modules.moduleTitle: Module 1: Full Stack Architecture & Node.js Basics

notes.heading: Client-Server Architecture Essentials
notes.overview: This lesson introduces client-server architecture in a practical way for MERN Stack. You will learn how React (Client) communicates with Express/Node (Server) via REST APIs.
keyPoints: Understand Request-Response cycle between Frontend and Backend
Role of HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
notes.codeExplanation: Demonstrates asynchronous data fetching from a client application to a backend server using Native Fetch API.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to handle asynchronous responses with .then() or async/await
Not handling CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) errors
notes.cheatsheetSummary: Clients request resources; servers process business logic and return data, usually in JSON format.

flashcards.question: What is the primary role of the client in MERN?
flashcards.answer: To render the user interface and send HTTP requests to the backend API.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain the difference between client-side rendering and server-side rendering.
interviewQuestions.answer: Client-side rendering builds HTML in the browser using JavaScript (like React), whereas server-side rendering delivers pre-built HTML from the server.

tasks.title: Task 1: Fetch External Data
tasks.problemStatement: Write a JavaScript function using `fetch` to retrieve user profiles from a public API.
tasks.hint: Use response.json() to convert the raw response to usable JSON.

tasks.title: Task 2: Handle Fetch Errors
tasks.problemStatement: Modify your fetch request to safely handle HTTP status errors using `try...catch`.
tasks.hint: Check `res.ok` to catch non-200 HTTP status codes.

notes.heading: Node.js Fundamentals
notes.overview: Learn about Node.js runtime, asynchronous event loops, and native modules like fs and path.
notes.codeExplanation: Asynchronously reads a file from disk using the Node.js built-in fs module.
commonMistakes: Using sync methods like `readFileSync` in production code blocking the main thread
notes.cheatsheetSummary: Node.js enables running JavaScript server-side with an event-driven, non-blocking model.

flashcards.question: What is the Node.js Event Loop?
flashcards.answer: A mechanism that handles asynchronous operations without blocking main execution thread.

interviewQuestions.question: Why is asynchronous programming important in Node.js?
interviewQuestions.answer: It allows handling thousands of concurrent requests efficiently on a single thread.

tasks.title: Task 1: Read File Content
tasks.problemStatement: Write a script using `fs.promises` to read data from `config.json`.

tasks.title: Task 2: Path Construction
tasks.problemStatement: Safely construct a cross-platform directory path using the `path` module.

modules.moduleTitle: Module 2: RESTful API Development with Express & MongoDB

notes.heading: Express.js REST APIs
notes.overview: Build dynamic backend routes, handle URL query params, and process POST payloads.
keyPoints: Handling GET, POST, PUT, DELETE operations
notes.codeExplanation: Sets up a standard Express API server returning structured JSON data.
notes.cheatsheetSummary: Express simplifies web server and REST API building on top of Node.js.

flashcards.question: What does express.json() middleware do?
flashcards.answer: Parses incoming requests with JSON payloads into req.body.

interviewQuestions.question: What is middleware in Express?
interviewQuestions.answer: Functions that process request/response objects before passing control to the next middleware.

tasks.title: Task 2: Parameterized Route

notes.heading: MongoDB & Mongoose ODM
notes.overview: Connect Express to MongoDB, define schemas, and execute CRUD queries using Mongoose.
notes.codeExplanation: Defines a structured database model schema for MongoDB users using Mongoose.
commonMistakes: Not handling database connection errors properly during server startup
notes.cheatsheetSummary: Mongoose acts as an Object Data Modeling (ODM) library for MongoDB and Node.js.

flashcards.question: What is a document in MongoDB?
flashcards.answer: A record in MongoDB structured as a JSON/BSON object.

interviewQuestions.question: Difference between Relational SQL and NoSQL MongoDB?
interviewQuestions.answer: SQL uses structured tables with fixed schemas, while MongoDB uses flexible document-based JSON structures.

tasks.title: Task 1: Define Mongoose Schema
tasks.problemStatement: Create a Product schema with `title` (String) and `price` (Number).

tasks.title: Task 2: Query Database Documents
tasks.problemStatement: Write an async function to fetch all products where price is greater than 50.

notes.heading: React Core Concepts
notes.overview: Learn functional components, JSX syntax, state management with useState, and side effects with useEffect.
notes.codeExplanation: Demonstrates interactive UI updates managed by React useState hook.
notes.expectedOutput: Renders interactive button incrementing count on click.
commonMistakes: Directly mutating state variables instead of calling setter functions
notes.cheatsheetSummary: React uses component-based architecture and Virtual DOM for high-performance rendering.

flashcards.question: What is Virtual DOM?
flashcards.answer: A lightweight copy of real DOM used by React to calculate efficient UI re-renders.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the purpose of key prop in React lists?
interviewQuestions.answer: Keys help React identify which items have changed, been added, or removed during list rendering.

tasks.title: Task 1: Toggle State Button
tasks.problemStatement: Build a React component toggling between 'ON' and 'OFF' text.

tasks.title: Task 2: API Integration in useEffect
tasks.problemStatement: Fetch user list on component mount and store inside state.
tasks.hint: Pass an empty array `[]` as dependency to useEffect.

notes.heading: Connecting React to Backend API
notes.overview: Connect React frontend with Express backend using JWT authentication and Axios HTTP calls.
keyPoints: JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for user auth
notes.codeExplanation: Sends authenticated requests passing JWT in HTTP Authorization header.
commonMistakes: Storing sensitive information inside decoded client-side JWT payload
notes.cheatsheetSummary: JWT allows stateless authentication between frontend client and backend API.

flashcards.question: What are 3 parts of a JWT?

interviewQuestions.question: Where should you store JWT on client-side?
interviewQuestions.answer: In httpOnly secure cookies to prevent XSS attacks, or in memory/localStorage depending on security trade-offs.

tasks.title: Task 1: Login Handler
tasks.problemStatement: Save authentication token to localStorage upon successful login.

tasks.title: Task 2: Protected Axios Client
tasks.problemStatement: Create an Axios instance automatically attaching Bearer token to requests.
